newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nan Ya up on unit's T$100 bln projects.
newsitem.headline: Nan Ya up on unit's T$100 bln projects.

text.p: Taiwan's Nan Ya Plastics rose at mid-morning on Monday after saying its Nan Ya Technology unit would invest more than T$100 billion over five years to build three microchip fabrication plants in northern Taiwan.
After 58 minutes at 0158 GMT, Nan Ya Plastics was up T$2 or 2.38 percent to T$86, while the overall index was up 1.16 percent.
"We plan to build three eight-inch or 12-inch wafer plants in the next five years in Linco town to strengthen our competitiveness," Nan Ya Plastics spokesman Wu Chia-chao told Reuters by telephone.

Nan Ya Technology, founded in 1994 to build a US$675 million dynamic random access memory chip plant, is wholly owned by Formosa Plastics group, with group member Nan Ya Plastics as key investor with a 56 percent stake.

The announcement was the fifth involving major wafermaking plants in three months, following announcements of huge projects by Taiwan's number one and two chipmakers, Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics.
"This proves again Taiwan's semiconductor industry really has the best outlook with so many huge investments ready to take off," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
"If conglomerates do not jump into the semiconductor industry, they will have no games to play in the next round," he said.
